8587: District of Summerland campground two blocks from Okanagan Lake, whose grassy, shaded sites lie near Eneas Creek (72 have power and water, 49 water only); it has a swing set and six public pickleball courts, and beaches, a spray park and a dog beach are within walking distance.  A sewer service is offered on Wednesdays or Thursdays (ask at the office), and the district's sani-dump is 3 km south.  Wood fires are not allowed; propane fire pits are.  The district gives its 2026 season as May 11 to mid-September. --Claude
8604: District of Tumbler Ridge campground in a creek setting on Flatbed Creek, 1 km from town, with fire pits, firewood, a cooking shelter, picnic areas, a playground, hiking trails and a swimming hole.  The district says it is open from May to September; the tourism site says May to October. --Claude
8608: Campground on the Sooke River owned and run by the non-profit Sooke Community Association, whose camping fees support the Sooke Community Hall and Art Morris Park, with water access for kayaking, paddleboarding and fishing, a small boat launch, a playground, a clubhouse and kitchen for events, and three rustic cabins; the Sooke Potholes and East Sooke Park are close by.  Only one site has a sewer hookup. --Claude
8641: Adults-only (18+) RV park along the Kootenay River in Castlegar, with landscaped grounds, mature trees and flowers, cable TV at every site, and walleye and trout fishing right outside the sites.  Stays of 28 days or more are taken all year. --Claude
8649: Resort beside the Oyster River near Black Creek on Vancouver Island, with a marina offering fishing charters and kayak and paddleboard rentals, a heated pool and pickleball courts, close to sandy beaches, tidal pools and the Oyster River Trail; it also rents cottages and stay-in-place RVs. --Claude
8665: Lakeshore campground on Summit Lake, 16 km southeast of Nakusp on Highway 6; its 39 deluxe sites have full hookups, and its waterfront sites power and water but no sewer.  Hot showers, laundry, boat moorage and boat rentals (tinners, canoes, kayaks and pedal boats) are free, and it has swim beaches and docks, boat docks and a launch, a fish-cleaning station for the trout-stocked lake, a dog beach and a fenced off-leash dog park, playgrounds, a kids' bike pump track, and access to hiking, biking, ATV and dirt-bike trails. --Claude
8677: Resort owned and run by the Kwakiutl First Nation on its ancestral land where the Cluxewe River meets Broughton Strait, near Port McNeill on northern Vancouver Island, with oceanfront, estuary and woodland sites, a boat ramp, a fish-cleaning station, a playground, barbecue rentals and beachfront cottages.  Generators are not allowed from May 1 to September 30.  A new water treatment plant made the resort's water safe to drink in June 2026. --Claude
8692: Resort on Knouff Lake, established in 1904 and one of the oldest in B.C., 45 minutes from Kamloops and 30 from Sun Peaks; it holds a North American fly-fishing record for a 17.5 lb dry-fly catch.  RV sites have power and water or no hookups at all, and there is a walk-in tent island, the Hideaway group site for up to five trailers, year-round rustic cabins fitted with cast-iron wood cook stoves, rental trailers, boat rentals and a family beach.  Wi-Fi reaches only the lodge; generators may run from 8 to 10 a.m. and 5 to 7 p.m., and the gate is closed overnight (10 p.m. to 8 a.m. in summer, 9 p.m. to 9 a.m. in winter). --Claude
8698: Forested campground on Highway 97A beside the Mara Foodliner store, 15 minutes south of Sicamous and 4 minutes from Mara Lake Provincial Beach and its boat launch, with brand-new washrooms and an outdoor shower in the trees.  Open from April to mid-October. --Claude
8762: Resort beside Takysie Lake, a lake of wild rainbow trout south of Burns Lake, with rustic lakeside cabins, guest docks, a boat launch, floatplane docking, a lakefront café, a market, a hardware store and gas station, a playground and a beach, and canoe, pedal boat, motorboat and party barge rentals.  Most RV sites have 20-amp power and a few 30-amp; the site water is cold only and is shut off by October 1, and the lake usually freezes from November to mid-April. --Claude
8783: RV park and campground at Mile 300 of the Alaska Highway in Fort Nelson, run by hosts Bryan and Janis Stanley, with open and shaded sites, large 30-amp pull-throughs, a few 50-amp back-ins and tent sites, a family restaurant, hard and soft ice cream, gift cabins of souvenirs, propane sales, a coin RV pressure wash and an electric-car charger; it is Starlink-friendly. --Claude
8947: Special Areas Board park 20 minutes south of Hanna on Highway 36, with well-treed sites for RVs of all sizes, a boat launch and a marina area that sells fuel, a beach, floating docks, a playground, basketball courts, a concession and hiking and biking trails.  Of its sites, 50 are reservable and 51 first-come, first-served. --Claude
9019: Town of Claresholm campground in Centennial Park, within walking distance of downtown, the Bridges at Claresholm golf course and the aquatic centre; a new shower building has change rooms and a camp kitchen, and there are horseshoe pits, ball diamonds, a playground and the town's spray park. --Claude
9033: Village of Rosemary campground with 3 full-service, 9 partial-service and 2 tent sites, a central fire pit and a gazebo; long stays are booked by phone. --Claude
9055: Village of Delia community campground beside the Delia Arena, at the base of the Hand Hills, with a playground and a picnic shelter; the water at the sites is seasonal.  The village takes bookings by phone until its own online reservation system is ready; its Campspot listing shows the campground closed indefinitely. --Claude
9066: Town of St. Paul campground north of the St. Paul Co-op Mall, beside the soccer fields, open from the May long weekend; 44 of its stalls have fire pits and tables, firewood is sold, and the large trout pond is open to the public for fishing daily from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. --Claude
9073: Town of Cardston campground by Lee Creek, run by a contractor, close to golf at the Lee Creek Valley course, trophy fishing, rafting and trail rides, and within reach of Waterton and Glacier national parks; it has a cabin and a reunion centre.  Early-season camping in April, when the water may not yet be on, is by arrangement; online booking opens in late April or early May. --Claude
9084: Family-owned campground in the town of Coaldale, a field bought and revitalized in 2020 that now has about 150 mature trees.  Attached to it are a mountain bike park of jumps and berms and an off-leash dog park with agility equipment, and it has walking and biking paths, a play area and a covered picnic shelter; a dozen restaurants are within walking distance. --Claude
9097: Private campground near Drayton Valley in Brazeau County, around a trout-stocked pond for catch-and-release fishing; it offers free kayaks, swimming, a driving range and three-hole pitch and putt, an entertainment area for movie nights, darts, ping pong and arcade games, and ATV access to the crown land across the range road.  The cabins are open all year and the RV and tent sites seasonally.  The campground's well water is not treated for drinking, so bring your own. --Claude
9102: Town of Penhold RV park beside the Penhold Regional Multiplex, a short walk from a grocery store and restaurants and near the town's pump track and skate park, splash park and disc golf course, with free washrooms, showers and laundry and a picnic table and fire pit at every site; seasonal sites are booked through the town office. --Claude
9103: RV-only resort on the grounds of Westerner Park in Red Deer, near shopping, golf courses and restaurants; 40 of its sites are fully winterized (15 of them 50-amp) and 46 have fire pits, and water and sewer hookups depend on the season and the site.  Its office is open from April to September and closed from October to March. --Claude
9112: Family-owned 27-hole golf course 15 minutes south of Camrose on Highway 21, with a large serviced campground, a clubhouse in a 1912 barn furnished in antiques, and a restaurant and lounge open to non-golfers.  Long weekends take a 3-night minimum. --Claude
9114: Campground of the Lacombe Legion (Branch 79) on Gull Lake near Bentley, gated and looked after by on-site caretakers, with two group sites, a beach, a boat launch, fish-cleaning stands, a camp kitchen, a picnic shelter and two playgrounds.  It opens on the May long weekend; bookings are online only and open on January 1. --Claude
9119: Family-run RV park of Ken and Leona Hood, 9 km west of Lloydminster on Highway 16 at Range Road 22, with a playground, a basketball hoop, a rec room of movies, books and board games, off-leash grass areas and central fire pits; it also stores RVs.  Online bookings of the drive-through sites are limited to 4 nights. --Claude
9120: Town of Coronation campground on the Coronation Dam reservoir, with newly built washrooms, group camping areas, a new playground and a camp kitchen to rent.  The reservoir holds rainbow trout and northern pike and has a launch for small fishing boats (12-volt electric motors only). --Claude
